title: Modest Mouse: The Band
description: From a small town outside Seattle to a No. 1 album: the people, the records and the stories behind Modest Mouse.

cards.prompt: In which small Washington town did Modest Mouse form?
cards.details: Issaquah sits in the foothills east of Seattle. Rain, pine trees and strip malls, all of which seep into the band's early songs.

cards.prompt: Issaquah is a short drive from which big Pacific Northwest city?
cards.details: Modest Mouse came up in the long shadow of the Seattle grunge explosion, but sounded nothing like it: twitchier, stranger, and more homemade.

cards.prompt: Modest Mouse's music is tied to which US region's indie scene?
cards.details: Alongside bands like Built to Spill and Death Cab for Cutie, they helped define the region's 1990s–2000s indie sound.

cards.prompt: How many founding members did Modest Mouse have?
cards.details: Isaac Brock, Jeremiah Green and Eric Judy: guitar and vocals, drums, and bass. The line-up grew a lot over the years.

cards.prompt: Who is Modest Mouse's frontman, guitarist and main songwriter?
cards.details: Brock's yelping, cracked-voice delivery and his lyrics about cosmic dread, sprawl and bad decisions *are* the Modest Mouse sound.
cards.hint: First name shares one with a son of Abraham

cards.prompt: Who was Modest Mouse's original drummer?
cards.details: Green's restless, jazzy drumming gave even the sloppiest early songs a pulse. He was with the band from the very start.

cards.prompt: Who played bass in the original Modest Mouse line-up?
cards.details: Judy's melodic basslines anchor many of the band's best-loved songs. He stayed for about two decades.

cards.prompt: The band's name comes from a phrase by which English writer?
cards.details: It comes from Woolf's description of "modest mouse-coloured people". Very literary origins for a band this rowdy.

cards.prompt: Which Virginia Woolf short story contains the "modest mouse-coloured people" line?
cards.details: A 1917 story in which the narrator lets her mind wander while staring at a mark on the wall. Fitting for a band of drifting, tangential lyrics.

cards.prompt: Complete the 1996 debut album title: "This Is a Long Drive for Someone with Nothing to ___"
cards.details: One of indie rock's great long titles, and a perfect summary of the record: long highway miles, boredom, and big thoughts.

cards.prompt: Which Seattle independent label put out Modest Mouse's first two albums?
cards.details: Up Records was a key Northwest indie label of the '90s. Modest Mouse stayed indie until the end of the decade.

cards.prompt: The song "Dramamine" from the debut album is named after a medicine for what?
cards.details: A very on-brand title for an album all about long, queasy drives.

cards.prompt: What is the band's 1997 second album, often hailed as their early masterpiece?
cards.details: A sprawling, furious record about strip malls, truck stops and the paving-over of the Pacific Northwest.

cards.prompt: Which song opens The Lonesome Crowded West?
cards.details: It lurches between whisper and scream. A great statement of intent for the whole album.

cards.prompt: Which 1999 compilation gathered Modest Mouse singles and EP tracks?
cards.details: A goldmine of non-album songs. For many fans it's as essential as the studio albums.

cards.prompt: Which 2000 album was the band's major-label debut?
cards.details: Bigger, colder and more cosmic: songs about space, death and the soul. Fans worried a major label would tame them. It didn't.

cards.prompt: Which major label signed Modest Mouse for The Moon & Antarctica?
cards.details: Epic stuck with them, and a few years later that patience paid off in a very big way.

cards.prompt: Which song opens The Moon & Antarctica?
cards.details: The third planet from the Sun is, of course, Earth. The song is a woozy, philosophical look at life on it.

cards.prompt: Who produced The Moon & Antarctica?
cards.details: Deck helped give the album its spacious, detailed sound. More headphones record than garage record.

cards.prompt: Which 2001 release finally put out the band's earliest mid-'90s recordings?
cards.details: A peek at the scrappy, lo-fi Modest Mouse from before the debut album.

cards.prompt: What was Isaac Brock's side project, which released Sharpen Your Teeth in 2002?
cards.details: A looser, eerier outlet for songs that didn't fit Modest Mouse.

cards.prompt: Complete the 2004 album title: "Good News for People Who Love ___"
cards.details: The record that took them from cult heroes to radio staples, without losing the weirdness.

cards.prompt: Which 2004 single became Modest Mouse's biggest hit?
cards.details: An unusually upbeat song for Brock: a shrug-it-off anthem that took the band onto mainstream radio and TV.

cards.prompt: Which other 2004 single, "The World at ___", came from Good News for People Who Love Bad News?
cards.details: "The World at Large" opens the album proper: a gentle, drifting song about moving on.

cards.prompt: Good News for People Who Love Bad News earned a Grammy nomination for best album in which genre?
cards.details: A big moment for a band that had spent the '90s on a small Seattle indie label.

cards.prompt: Which drummer stepped in on Good News while Jeremiah Green took a break from the band?
cards.details: Green stepped away in 2003 and came back the following year.

cards.prompt: Benjamin Weikel also drummed in which Oregon band?
cards.details: The Helio Sequence is a duo from the Portland area. Weikel was a natural fit as a Northwest indie drummer.

cards.prompt: Which twangy instrument does Isaac Brock pick up on songs like "Satin in a Coffin"?
cards.details: Brock's banjo gives some of the band's darkest songs a creaky, back-porch-at-midnight feel.

cards.prompt: Which legendary guitarist joined Modest Mouse in 2006?
cards.details: A genuine indie legend joining a band that grew up on his records. Fans could hardly believe it.

cards.prompt: Before Modest Mouse, Johnny Marr was the guitarist in which famous Manchester band?
cards.details: His chiming, jangly guitar work with The Smiths in the 1980s influenced a whole generation of indie bands.

cards.prompt: Which 2007 album was Modest Mouse's first to debut at No. 1 in the US?
cards.answer: We Were Dead Before the Ship Even Sank
cards.details: Topping the Billboard 200 with an album this odd and seafaring was a huge win for weird music. See the companion set for more.

cards.prompt: Johnny Marr went on to join which band, from Wakefield in England, after Modest Mouse?
cards.details: Marr's time in Modest Mouse lasted only a few years, but he played on one of their most successful albums.

cards.prompt: Which 2009 EP gathered leftover songs from the Good News and We Were Dead sessions?
cards.answer: No One's First, and You're Next
accept: No One's First and You're Next
No Ones First and Youre Next
cards.details: Proof that the band's leftovers are better than a lot of bands' singles.

cards.prompt: What is the name of Isaac Brock's own record label imprint?
cards.details: Brock has used it to put out records by other artists. The name could double as a joke about how slowly Modest Mouse albums arrive (see the next card).

cards.prompt: Which founding member left Modest Mouse in the early 2010s?
cards.details: That left Brock and Green as the two remaining original members.

cards.prompt: Which 2015 album ended an eight-year wait for a new Modest Mouse record?
cards.details: Eight years between albums: "glacial pace" indeed. It was worth the wait for most fans.

cards.prompt: Which song was the lead single from Strangers to Ourselves?
cards.details: A bouncy, catchy single that showed the band hadn't lost its bite after eight years away.

cards.prompt: What is Modest Mouse's 2021 studio album?
cards.details: Their first album of the 2020s, and proof the band was still making strange, restless records nearly 30 years in.

cards.prompt: In which year did founding drummer Jeremiah Green die?
cards.details: Green died of cancer at the very end of 2022. He had drummed with the band since the very beginning, and fans remember him as its heartbeat.
